examples.en: I wear comfortable leggings when I exercise.
These leggings stretch well, so they are comfortable.
The leggings were small, so I changed them to a bigger size.
I wore a long T-shirt over black leggings.

examples.ko: 동생이 새 레깅스도 사고 양말도 샀어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling bought new leggings and socks too.
I came to yoga class after changing into leggings.

explain: 바지처럼 '입다'와 같이 써요. 영어 leggings처럼 s가 붙은 모양이지만 한국어는 복수 표시가 따로 없어서 하나든 여러 개든 '레깅스'예요. 헐렁한 '바지'와 달리 몸에 붙는 옷을 말할 때 써요.

phrases.example: 오늘은 검은 레깅스에 긴 티셔츠를 입었어요.
phrases.en: Today I wore black leggings and a long T-shirt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색을 넣어서 어떤 레깅스인지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add a color to say which leggings you mean.

phrases.en: I bought a pair of leggings to work out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷은 '벌'로 세요. 한 벌이어도 '레깅스'는 그대로예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Clothes are counted with '벌'. The word 레깅스 stays the same for one pair.

phrases.en: I bought leggings at the department store.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쇼핑할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase when shopping.

explain_en: Loanword — stretchy tight pants, sportswear or casual. Like '바지', it goes with the verb '입다'. It looks plural in English, but Korean has no plural marker, so 레깅스 is used for one pair or many. You use it for a close-fitting garment, unlike a loose '바지'.

t90.ax: I wore a long T-shirt over black leggings.

examples.en: Mornings and evenings are chilly, so I bought a windbreaker.

examples.ko: 바람막이는 가볍고 얇아서 가방에 쏙 들어가요.
examples.en: A windbreaker is light and thin, so it fits easily in a bag.

examples.ko: 바람막이 점퍼를 입으니까 바람이 하나도 안 느껴져요.
examples.en: With a windbreaker jacket on, I can't feel any wind.

examples.ko: 집 앞의 큰 나무가 바람막이가 되어 줘요.
examples.en: The big tree in front of the house acts as a windbreak.

examples.ko: 이 바람막이에 모자가 달려 있어서 비 올 때도 좋아요.
examples.en: This windbreaker has a hood, so it's good when it rains too.

examples.ko: 바람막이로 쓸 만한 얇은 겉옷을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a thin jacket that works as a windbreaker.

explain: 옷으로는 '바람막이 점퍼'를 줄여서 그냥 '바람막이'라고 해요. 바람을 막아 주는 나무나 벽 같은 것도 '바람막이'라고 불러요.

phrases.en: In autumn, one windbreaker jacket is enough.
phrases.nuance_ko: '바람막이'의 전체 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the full name of 바람막이.

phrases.en: It was windy, so I went out in a windbreaker.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷은 '입다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Clothes go with '입다'.

phrases.en: If you're cold, throw on a windbreaker.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가볍게 겉에 입는 느낌일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives a feeling of casually putting it on over other clothes.

explain_en: As clothing, '바람막이 점퍼' is shortened to just '바람막이'. Trees or walls that block the wind are also called '바람막이'.

en: frame of a pair of glasses

examples.en: These frames are thin, so they're light and comfortable.
I changed the frame color from black to brown.

examples.ko: 얼굴이 둥글어서 각진 안경테가 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: My face is round, so angular frames suit me well.
The frame was bent, so I took it to the optician's.

examples.ko: 안경테만 새로 사고 렌즈는 그대로 썼어요.
examples.en: I bought only new frames and kept the same lenses.
Expensive frames don't break easily.

explain: 렌즈(안경알)를 제외한 틀 부분이에요. 귀에 거는 부분은 따로 '안경다리'라고 불러요. 안경을 고를 때는 '테'와 '렌즈'를 따로 골라요.

phrases.en: I picked glasses frames that suit my face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안경을 살 때 틀을 선택하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes choosing the frame when buying glasses.

phrases.en: I find thin frames light and comfortable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 틀의 모양이나 두께를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the shape or thickness of the frame.

phrases.en: I sat on it and the frame got bent.
phrases.nuance_ko: 틀이 구부러져서 모양이 변했을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the frame gets bent out of shape.

explain_en: It is the frame part of glasses, without the lenses ('안경알'). The part that goes over the ears is called '안경다리' separately. When buying glasses, you choose the frame and the lenses separately.

examples.en: I made kimchi stew with pork foreleg meat.

examples.ko: 고양이가 앞다리를 쭉 뻗고 기지개를 켰어요.
examples.en: The cat stretched out its front legs and had a good stretch.
The puppy scratched my knee with its front paw.
The horse raised its front legs and neighed loudly.
A rabbit's hind legs are much longer than its front legs.
Since falling, the puppy has been limping on its front leg.

explain: 주로 동물의 앞쪽 다리를 말하고, 반대말은 '뒷다리'예요. 사람의 팔은 '앞다리'라고 하지 않고 '팔'이라고 해요. 요리에서는 '앞다리살'이라는 고기 부위 이름으로도 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Front-leg pork is cheap, so it's good for stew.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고기 부위 이름으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used as the name of a cut of meat.

phrases.en: The puppy raises its front paw to say hello.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물이 앞쪽 다리를 올리는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes an animal lifting its front leg.

phrases.en: A horse has strong front and back legs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물의 다리를 앞뒤로 나눠서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about an animal's legs front and back.

explain_en: It mainly means the front legs of an animal, and the opposite is '뒷다리'. A person's arm is just called '팔', not '앞다리'. It also appears often in cooking as the meat cut '앞다리살'.

examples.en: I wore jeans for the bottoms.
I matched the colors of the top and bottom.
This store sells bottoms separately.
The bottoms are too long, so I need to have them shortened.
I wear comfortable bottoms when I exercise.
A stain got on the bottoms, so I took them to the laundry.

explain: '상의'(윗옷)의 짝말이에요. 바지와 치마를 함께 가리키는 말이라 옷 가게나 쇼핑몰에서 볼 수 있어요. 일상 대화에서는 '바지', '치마'처럼 구체적인 이름을 써도 돼요.

phrases.en: I bought the top and the bottom separately.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗옷과 아래옷을 함께 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The paired term for top and bottom clothing.

phrases.en: I wore comfortable bottoms today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바지나 치마를 입는다는 뜻이고 '입다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with 입다 for putting on pants or a skirt.

phrases.en: What is your bottom size?
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷 가게에서 바지나 치마 크기를 물을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in shops when asking about pants or skirt size.

explain_en: It is the partner of '상의' (top). It covers pants and skirts together, so you see it in clothing shops and online stores. In everyday talk you can use specific words like '바지' or '치마'.

examples.en: A small diamond is set in the ring.
That diamond is very expensive.
He gave his wife a diamond ring.
It's hard to tell a fake diamond apart.
I saw a necklace made of diamonds.
This watch has diamonds in it too.

explain: '다이아몬드'를 줄인 말이라서 대화에서 편하게 써요. 카드 게임에서 ◆ 모양의 카드도 '다이아'라고 불러요.

phrases.en: That ring has a big diamond.
phrases.nuance_ko: '다이아'의 원래 말이고, 조금 더 격식 있게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The full form of 다이아, sounding a bit more formal.

phrases.en: My husband gave me a diamond ring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다이아가 박힌 반지를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a ring set with a diamond.

phrases.en: This is a fake diamond, so it's cheap.
phrases.nuance_ko: 진짜가 아닌 것을 말할 때 '가짜'를 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put '가짜' in front for something that isn't real.

explain_en: It is a shortened form of 다이아몬드, so it is handy in casual talk. The ◆ suit in card games is also called 다이아.

examples.ko: 동네 쌀집에서 쌀 한 포대를 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a sack of rice at the neighborhood rice shop.

examples.ko: 쌀집 아저씨가 쌀을 집까지 배달해 줬어요.
examples.en: The man from the rice shop delivered the rice to my house.
The number of rice shops has dropped a lot these days.

examples.ko: 쌀집에 가면 잡곡도 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you go to a rice shop, you can also buy mixed grains.

examples.ko: 우리 집 앞에는 오래된 쌀집이 하나 있어요.
examples.en: There is an old rice shop in front of my house.
The rice shop sells freshly milled rice.

explain: '쌀가게'도 같은 곳을 가리켜요. '쌀집 아저씨'처럼 가게 주인을 편하게 부를 때도 써요.

phrases.en: I bought rice at the rice shop in front of my house.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쌀집'과 같은 곳이에요. '쌀집'이 말할 때 더 편하게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same place as 쌀집; 쌀집 sounds a bit more casual in speech.

phrases.en: The owner of the rice store is very kind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게를 하는 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the person who runs the store.

phrases.en: I went to the rice store and ordered rice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쌀을 사러 갈 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when going to buy rice.
phrases.en_equiv: to go to the rice store

explain_en: '쌀가게' refers to the same kind of place. People also use it casually for the owner, as in '쌀집 아저씨'.

t90.ax: The rice shop sells freshly milled rice.

examples.en: My monthly income is enough to cover living expenses.
My monthly income is unstable, so I'm worried.
I save about half of my monthly income.
The rent is too expensive compared to my monthly income.
If you add up the couple's monthly income, it's quite comfortable.

examples.ko: 월수입 대비 지출을 매달 적어 봐요.
examples.en: I write down my spending against my monthly income every month.

explain: '월급'은 회사에서 받는 돈이고, '월수입'은 장사나 부업 등을 포함해 한 달에 버는 돈 전체를 말할 수 있어요. 말할 때는 '한 달 수입'이라고도 해요. '월수입이 많다/적다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: What is your monthly income?
phrases.nuance_ko: 대화에서 '월수입'을 풀어서 쉽게 말한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain spoken way to say 월수입 in conversation.

phrases.en: My monthly income went up because I started a new job.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 달에 버는 돈이 많아졌다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the money earned each month has increased.

phrases.en: My monthly income is low, so it's hard to save.
phrases.nuance_ko: '월수입이 많다'의 반대 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite use of 월수입이 많다.

explain_en: Income received per month. '월급' is the pay you receive from a company, while '월수입' can include everything you earn in a month, such as business or side jobs. In speech people also say '한 달 수입'. You say '월수입이 많다/적다'.

examples.ko: 이번 달 전기료가 너무 많이 나왔어요.
examples.en: This month's electricity bill came out really high.

examples.ko: 여름에는 에어컨 때문에 전기료가 두 배로 올라요.
examples.en: In summer the power bill doubles because of the air conditioner.

examples.ko: 전기료를 아끼려고 안 쓰는 플러그를 뽑아요.
examples.en: I unplug things I'm not using to save on the electricity bill.
Do you pay the electricity bill by automatic transfer every month?

examples.ko: 겨울에도 난방 때문에 전기료 걱정이 커요.
examples.en: Even in winter I worry about the power bill because of the heating.
The electricity bill notice came in the mailbox today.

explain: '전기 요금'을 줄인 말이고, 일상에서는 '전기세'라고도 말해요. '전기료가 나오다', '전기료를 내다', '전기료를 아끼다'처럼 '나오다·내다·아끼다'와 자주 같이 써요.

phrases.en: This month's electricity bill went up.
phrases.nuance_ko: '전기료'의 원래 말이고, 안내문이나 뉴스에서 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: The full form of '전기료', often seen in notices and news.

phrases.en: The electricity bill is high in winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A word used often in everyday conversation.

phrases.en: I turn off the lights to save on electricity.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 덜 쓰려고 할 때 '아끼다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '아끼다' when trying to spend less.
phrases.en_equiv: to save on the electricity bill

explain_en: Standard word for the electricity fee, used on bills and in writing. It is a short form of '전기 요금', and in daily talk people also say '전기세'. It often goes with verbs like '나오다' (to come out), '내다' (to pay) and '아끼다' (to save), as in '전기료가 나오다'.

t90.ax: This month's electricity bill came out really high.

examples.en: The bicycle chain came off.
I put the chain on the door and slept.
On snowy roads you put chains on the tires.
I received a chain necklace as a gift.

examples.ko: 이 커피 체인은 전국에 가게가 있어요.
examples.en: This coffee chain has stores all over the country.
The owner of the chain store manages the shop personally.

explain: 자전거 체인처럼 쇠고리를 말하기도 하고, 같은 이름의 가게가 여러 곳에 있는 '체인점'을 말하기도 해요. 가게는 '프랜차이즈'라고도 하지만 일상에서는 '체인점'이라고 흔히 말해요.

phrases.en: This coffee shop has chain stores all over the country.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 이름의 가게가 여러 곳에 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for shops with the same name in many places.

phrases.en: The bicycle chain broke.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쇠고리가 끊어졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a metal chain breaks.

phrases.en: I put the chain on the door at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문을 잠그는 쇠고리를 걸 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for putting a door chain on to lock the door.

explain_en: Loanword — bike chains, restaurant or hotel chains (체인점) It can mean a metal chain, like a bike chain, or a group of stores under the same name, a '체인점'. Another word for such stores is '프랜차이즈', but '체인점' is the common everyday term.

examples.en: It's better to care about substance than appearance.
Even if it looks great outside, the inside matters.
This fruit doesn't look good, but it tastes delicious.
Don't judge just by outward appearance.
They only changed the outside, so it looks like a new car.
The two products look alike on the outside, so I got confused.

explain: '겉모습'과 거의 같고, 물건이나 음식의 바깥 모양을 말할 때 잘 어울려요. 사람에게는 '겉모습'이나 '외모'도 써요. 반대로 안쪽은 '속'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: Don't judge a person only by their outward appearance.
phrases.nuance_ko: '겉모양'과 거의 같은 뜻이고, 사람에게도 자연스럽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as 겉모양, and it can also be used naturally for people.

phrases.example: 이 빵은 겉모양이 예뻐서 선물하기 좋아요.
phrases.en: This bread looks pretty, so it's good for a gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이나 물건의 바깥 모양을 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise how a food or object looks on the outside.

phrases.en: Unlike how it looks, the taste is ordinary.
phrases.nuance_ko: 보이는 모습과 실제가 다를 때 이어서 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the real thing differs from how it looks.

explain_en: Outer form or look of objects, like fruit (겉모양이 예쁘다) It is almost the same as '겉모습' and fits the outer look of objects and food. For people, '겉모습' or '외모' is also used. The inside is called '속'.

t90.ax: Don't judge just by outward appearance.

en: to be performed; to be staged

examples.ko: 이 뮤지컬은 매일 저녁 서울에서 공연돼요.
examples.en: This musical is performed in Seoul every evening.
That play was staged in Seoul last month.

examples.ko: 새 콘서트가 다음 달부터 공연될 거예요.
examples.en: The new concert will be performed starting next month.

examples.ko: 공연되는 동안에는 사진을 찍으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not take photos while it is being performed.

examples.ko: 학교 강당에서 학생 연극이 공연되면 보러 갈래요?
examples.en: If a student play is staged in the school hall, do you want to go see it?

examples.ko: 이 작품은 세계 여러 나라에서 공연되고 있어요.
examples.en: This work is being performed in many countries around the world.

explain: '공연하다'는 무대에서 연주하거나 연기하는 쪽이고, '공연되다'는 작품이 무대에 올라가는 것이에요. 영화는 '상영되다', TV와 라디오는 '방송되다'라고 구분해요. 뮤지컬·연극·콘서트·발레에 잘 어울려요.

phrases.example: 그 연극이 지금 대학로에서 공연되고 있어요.
phrases.en: That play is being performed in Daehangno right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 있다'를 붙여 지금 무대에 올라가는 중이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-고 있다' means it is currently on stage.

phrases.example: 다음 달에 새 뮤지컬이 공연될 예정이에요.
phrases.en: A new musical is scheduled to be performed next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '예정이다'와 함께 앞으로의 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '예정이다', it talks about a scheduled plan.

phrases.example: 공연된 작품 중에서 이게 제일 좋았어요.
phrases.en: Of the works that were performed, this one was the best.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸며서 '무대에 올라간'이라는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It modifies a noun, adding the sense of 'staged'.

explain_en: Passive; a play, concert or show is put on for an audience. '공연하다' is the side performing on stage; '공연되다' is a work being put on stage. Movies are '상영되다', and TV and radio are '방송되다'. It fits musicals, plays, concerts and ballet.

dis.h: a show or concert is staged

p.n: 상연되다 is more written and formal; it also covers films.

t90.ax: That play was staged in Seoul last month.

examples.en: My younger sibling attends a national university.
National universities tend to have lower tuition than private ones.
A professor from a national university came to give a special lecture.

examples.ko: 우리 지역 국립대가 새 캠퍼스를 열었어요.
examples.en: Our region's national university opened a new campus.

examples.ko: 국립대와 사립대 중 어디가 더 좋아요?
examples.en: Which is better, a national or a private university?
I graduated from a national university and work in my hometown.

phrases.en: I want to enter a national university next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대학에 들어가는 이야기를 할 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for talking about getting into a university.

phrases.en: I am a national university student.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기소개나 사람을 소개할 때 '국립대' 뒤에 '학생'을 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 'student' after the word, used when introducing yourself or others.

phrases.en: My older sister graduated from a national university.
phrases.nuance_ko: '국립대'의 줄이지 않은 말이에요. 조금 더 격식 있는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The full, unshortened form of the word, which sounds a bit more formal.

explain_en: University run by the state (서울대 등); contrasts with private. It is a shortened form of '국립대학교'. Its opposite is '사립대' (private university).

examples.ko: 이 책은 청소년 독자층을 겨냥해서 만들었어요.
examples.en: This book was made with teenage readers in mind.
The readership is broad, so anyone can read it easily.
The new novel is popular among readers in their twenties.

examples.ko: 독자층에 따라 글의 말투를 바꿔야 해요.
examples.en: You have to change the tone of the writing depending on the readership.
The readership is gradually getting older.

examples.ko: 독자층도 달라서 두 책의 분위기가 달라요.
examples.en: The readerships differ too, so the two books feel different.

explain: '독자'는 읽는 사람 하나하나이고, '독자층'은 나이나 취향이 비슷한 읽는 사람들의 무리예요. 책, 잡지, 웹툰을 이야기할 때 '독자층이 넓다/좁다'로 자주 써요.

phrases.en: This magazine has a wide readership.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 사람이 읽는다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means many kinds of people read it.

phrases.en: It's a specialist book, so the readership is narrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: '넓다'의 반대로, 읽는 사람이 한정될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 넓다, used when the readers are limited.

phrases.en: This webtoon has many young readers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에 나이나 특징을 붙여 어떤 독자인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put an age or trait before it to say what kind of readers.

explain_en: '독자' means individual readers, while '독자층' is a group of readers with similar age or taste. It is often used with books, magazines and webtoons, as in '독자층이 넓다/좁다'.

examples.en: The new phone has a very bright display.
The staff changed the product display in the store.
The battery status appears on the display.
There is a model inside the glass display.

examples.ko: 디스플레이는 크기가 너무 작은 것 같아요.
examples.en: The display seems too small.
The display looked nice, so I went into the shop.

explain: 화면 장치도, 가게에서 물건을 보기 좋게 늘어놓는 일도 디스플레이라고 해요. 장치는 '화면', 늘어놓는 일은 '진열'로 바꿔 말할 수 있어요.

phrases.en: The phone screen is too small.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장치의 디스플레이는 말할 때 보통 '화면'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: For the device, people usually say '화면' in speech.

phrases.en: The product display at the shop entrance is pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게에서 물건을 보기 좋게 늘어놓는 일은 '진열'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '진열' is the word for arranging goods in a shop.

phrases.en: This computer has a big display.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장치의 화면 크기를 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for talking about the size of a device screen.

explain_en: Both a screen device and the arrangement of goods in a shop are called 'diseupeullei'. The device can be said as '화면' and the arranging as '진열'.
